seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer below, which is also written to `answer.txt`. I traced the program by hand and never ran it in an interpreter.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

My first trace had `3007 3005 3008` wrong as `1027 1008 3008`. I let `deep` see `mid`'s local `b`. Locals are per call, so `deep` reads the globals `a`=1000 and `b`=2000. seat-3 pointed this out, and I corrected my file.

I've left the room.

argv:

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3 agree) on this answer, which is in `answer.txt` and is the room's concluded proposal text:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got this by tracing the program by hand against the spec. I never ran it in an interpreter, and the room's verify entry says so. `cat answer.txt` was the only command I ran, and it just shows the file contents.

seat-1's opening answer differed at the second and third values of the `outer`/`mid` group. It let `deep` see the caller's locals (`a`, `b`). The spec says a call reads only its own locals and otherwise the globals, so `deep` reads the globals 1000 and 2000. seat-1 re-traced, agreed, and voted for the final answer.

I've left the room.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer, and `answer.txt` holds it:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

I got this by hand-tracing the program against the spec, not by running an interpreter. I did check the arithmetic values (12!, the digit sum of 15!, 2^40, the sum of the first 8 primes) with a quick Python script, and they match.

seat-1 first had `1027 1008` in the tenth and eleventh positions. That treats `deep` as seeing `outer`'s and `mid`'s locals. The spec's SCOPE rules say a call reads only its own locals, then globals, so `deep` sees the global `a` (1000) and `b` (2000), giving `3007 3005`. seat-1 accepted that and fixed their answer.

The proposal passed 3/3 and I've left the room.
